label: PF Backlog 435
title: B5: Rust protected components

analysis.implementation_strategy: No candidate existing code is identified, so this is a new capability. However, reuse-first principles apply: identify which Go-core components are candidates for Rust protection (e.g. execution engine hot paths, credential handling, crypto). Build FFI boundaries (cgo) between Go core and Rust protected modules. Follow the trigger explicitly: this item activates only when a measured security or performance need is identified, so the implementation strategy starts with a measurement/profiling phase, then isolates the specific hot-path or security-critical component into Rust. Leverage the compiled-artifact edition pipeline (BI-PF-0388) for distribution.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-0391 (Epic B) architecture decisions on Rust scope and toolchain.
RELATED BI-PF-0405 (WASM plugins) — both need Rust/WASM toolchain; share build infra.
RELATED BI-PF-0388 — compiled-editions pipeline must support Rust artifacts.
conflict_findings: Potential build-system conflict with BI-PF-0405: both introduce Rust toolchain into the build. Coordinate toolchain version, target profiles, and CI jobs.
No other item in this batch touches Go core execution engine.
duplication_findings: No existing Rust components in the codebase — no duplication.
BI-PF-0405 (WASM plugins) will also involve Rust toolchain; coordinate Rust build infrastructure to share setup.
BI-PF-0406 (service decomposition) may isolate services in a way that reduces the need for Rust-protected in-process components; ensure Rust boundary is compatible with future service split.
analysis.rationale: This item is gated by a measurement trigger that has not yet been satisfied. No existing code is identified to extend, making this a new capability. The main risk is premature adoption. It should remain at lower priority until the trigger is met.
assumptions: A specific hot-path or security-critical component can be identified through profiling/measurement before Rust migration.
Go core is the primary runtime (per BI-PF-0388 ADR).
Rust component is compiled once and linked via cgo or loaded as a shared library.
The compiled-edition pipeline (BI-PF-0388) can incorporate Rust build artifacts.
risks: Premature Rust adoption: moving code to Rust adds complexity, build time, and maintenance burden without proven benefit.
FFI boundary bugs: Go↔Rust FFI is a source of subtle memory/ownership bugs.
Trigger ambiguity: 'measured security/perf need' has no threshold defined; may never trigger or may trigger too early.
Team Rust proficiency may be limited; hiring/training cost.
evidence: Item body trigger: 'measured security/perf need' — implies a gate before implementation.
No candidate existing code confirmed — greenfield Rust component.
BI-PF-0388 ADR confirms Go core as the primary runtime.
